verdict.rationale: Letta's own self-hosting docs say agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control. The self-hosted App Server runs on a central, always-on machine, and agent state, including memory, stays on-device with no Letta account required. However, the evidence never states the self-hostable code is open source, never mentions Docker, and shared memory repositories are hosted in Letta Cloud, so the story is not fully covered. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license or source-build path, Docker or container deployment docs, a self-hosted option for shared memory (currently Letta Cloud-hosted), and independent hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Letta agents can run entirely on infrastructure you control
Run the Letta App Server to host local agents on a central, always-on machine and expose them to client applications through the Agent SDK
all agent state, including messages, memory, and provider connections, stays on-device, and no Letta account is required.
The Letta App Server lets you deploy the Letta agent harness as a service.
